compound.name: luteolin
compound.one_liner: Flavone aglycone of sage and thyme; in plants mostly present as glycosides such as luteolin-7-glucoside.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Salvia officinalis L., folium and Salvia officinalis L., aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/150801/2015 (20 Sep 2016). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-salvia-officinalis-l-folium-and-salvia-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: LUTEOLIN Leaf and Shoot, no values. EMA: flavonoids ~1.1 % total, luteolin and apigenin and their glycosides listed without individual %.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Thymus vulgaris L., Thymus zygis L., herba. EMA/HMPC/342334/2013 (12 Nov 2013). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-thymus-vulgaris-l-vulgaris-zygis-l-herba_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: EMA: luteolin '1.12 mg/g in the herbal substance, 3.9 mg/g in a dry extract ..., 0.466 mg/g in the liquid extract'. Duke: LUTEOLIN Leaf, Plant (no values). Kosakowska 2020 reports luteolin 7-O-glucoside 46.77-325.11 mg/100 g DW in 'Standard Winter'. | Basis as recorded: dried herbal substance

occurrences.source_citation: Kosakowska O, et al. (2021) Antioxidant and antibacterial activity of essential oils and hydroethanolic extracts of Greek oregano (O. vulgare L. subsp. hirtum (Link) Ietswaart) and common oregano (O. vulgare L. subsp. vulgare). Molecules 26(4):988
occurrences.note: Reported as glycosides: see luteolin-7-glucoside. Aglycone not verified: no Duke/KNApSAcK record; the paper found luteolin 7-O-glucoside as the dominant flavonoid of the hirtum extract but did not quantify free luteolin.

compound.absorption_bioavailability: Not researched for luteolin specifically; flavone glycosides generally need hydrolysis before absorption and are then extensively conjugated (shown for apigenin) [44].
compound.teaching_note: The aglycone is what databases list; the plant mostly stores the glucoside, which is why oregano points to luteolin-7-glucoside instead.
gaps: Oregano: reported as glycosides only; free luteolin row verified:false.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
